title: Elevator state machine and flows
idea: The elevator lifecycle is a state machine: a car moves between IDLE, MOVING, DOORS_OPEN and OUT_OF_SERVICE only along allowed arrows, so it never moves with open doors.
points: IDLE starts MOVING for a call elsewhere, or opens doors for one here.
MOVING may only stop with DOORS_OPEN, or halt as OUT_OF_SERVICE.
Doors must close, back to IDLE, before the car moves again.
Only an operator returns an OUT_OF_SERVICE car to IDLE.

code.title: State enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Elevator asks the enum before changing state.

walk.text: A normal stop. The try to move with doors open is refused.
An emergency stop. The car stays out until an operator restores it.
An EnumMap lists the allowed next states for each state.
`canMoveTo` is the one question every transition asks.
Refuse and report an illegal move; otherwise record the new state.

pitfalls: Do not set `state` from many places; every change goes through `moveTo`.
Never allow DOORS_OPEN to MOVING directly; doors close to IDLE first.
Keep Direction apart from ElevatorState; an IDLE car can still face UP.

quiz.q: What does the seventh line of ElevatorLifecycle print?
quiz.why: OUT_OF_SERVICE allows only IDLE next. `canMoveTo(MOVING)` is false, so `moveTo` prints the refusal and keeps the state.

takeaway: Write allowed transitions once, in the enum; refuse everything else.

starters: Should door reopening (someone blocks the door) be its own state?
Would the State pattern fit better than an enum here?
How do I log every transition for maintenance audits?
